proposed_fix.description: After confirming CPU throttling on the currencyservice container, raise its CPU limit modestly (requests unchanged) via a human-approved change, then watch latency and CPU.
steps: Check the currencyservice pod's CPU throttling (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total ratio) and current CPU requests/limits against actual usage.
Check the currencyservice_diskio deviation (E1/E4, z~4e12) for a possible metric artifact or a separate disk I/O problem, so the CPU change is not applied to the wrong cause.
Check the node's kernel version, as R1 suggests, for known CFS throttling bugs.
If throttling is confirmed, propose a modest increase to the currencyservice container CPU limit only (requests unchanged), applied to one replica or a canary first, after on-call approval.
Monitor currencyservice_cpu, latency-50/90 and frontend/checkoutservice latency for 15-30 minutes. Continue the rollout only if latency improves.
preconditions: Throttling is confirmed on the currencyservice container, not just high CPU usage.
The cluster or node has spare CPU capacity for the larger limit.
A human has approved the change and the previous resource spec is recorded.
Another alert or symptom is firing for this service (latency deviations in E1/E4 qualify), per R1's guidance on raising limits.
proposed_fix.rollback: Revert the currencyservice deployment to the previously recorded CPU limit (kubectl rollout undo or reapply the prior manifest) and confirm the pods restart with the original resources.
